meta.name: Nios II
meta.description: A Nios II/s processor (Logisim-evolution's Nios2s simulator): one instruction per rising clock edge, its fetches and data accesses go over its SoC bus; the IRQ pins feed ipending directly and custom instructions use the pins on the top edge

bus.label: Bus
bus.title: The SoC bus the processor uses for its instructions and data (Logisim-evolution's Connected bus)

resetVector.label: Reset vector (hex)
resetVector.title: Address of the first instruction after a reset when no program has been loaded (a loaded program starts at its entry point)

exceptionVector.label: Exception vector (hex)
exceptionVector.title: Where hardware interrupts and trap go (Logisim-evolution: 0x14 by default)

breakVector.label: Break vector (hex)
breakVector.title: Where the break instruction goes (Logisim-evolution: 0x30 by default)

irqWidth.label: IRQ inputs
irqWidth.title: Number of interrupt inputs (0 to 32); IRQi is bit i of ipending (enabled by ienable)

stateVisible.label: Show state
stateVisible.title: Off draws only a grey box on the body, which is faster while the processor runs

program.label: Program
program.title: Run controls, loading a program (ELF file or assembler) and the loaded program with breakpoints

status.label: Status
status.title: Run state, program counter and why the processor stopped

status.notConnected: Not connected to a bus: choose one in the Bus attribute

asm.title: Assembler: {{name}}
asm.template:
# Nios II program. It is assembled and written over the CPU's bus,
# so a SoC Memory must answer at these addresses.
        .text
        .org 0x0
_start:
        movi r2, 0          # sum
        movi r3, 1          # i
        movi r4, 10
loop:
        add  r2, r2, r3
        addi r3, r3, 1
        ble  r3, r4, loop
end:
        br   end            # stays here: r2 = 55
